clue.text: Courage may end with pain

definitions.meaning: boldness or daring, as in having the cheek to do something
a fibre carrying sensation through the body, whose endings register hurt

explanation.surface: Bravery in a hard situation might finish in suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'nerve endings': the bodily fibre is something that may end with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the nerve to do something means having the daring or boldness to do it.

clue.text: Chorus for Christmas present at length where you can't get water?

parts.note: now means at present
an ell is an old measure of length
a place with no well has no water

explanation.surface: A carol refrain about a long-drawn-out present in a waterless place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. The second half reads as 'no well', the place without water.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Nowell is a traditional carol whose refrain repeats the old word for Christmas.

clue.text: Relics raised in part with money

indicators.note: in places the upturned relics within the word for a part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the relics are written bottom to top

parts.note: the bones of saints are kept as relics

explanation.surface: Holy remains lifted as part of a fundraising effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suits a down clue, where the relics are written upwards inside the part. The rose noble was a medieval English gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose noble was a medieval English gold coin, a piece of currency stamped with a rose.

clue.text: Some brief fragments hidden in London

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Short scraps of something buried somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Effra is one of London's lost rivers, now running underground in culverts and sewers, so 'hidden' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This lost South London river now flows entirely underground, so it is literally out of sight beneath the city.

clue.text: Reversal of persecutor in reputation may be Christian

indicators.note: in places the turned-round emperor inside the word for reputation

parts.note: fame is renown or reputation

indicators.note: Reversal of tells us the persecutor's name is read from right to left

parts.note: the emperor Nero famously persecuted the early Christians

explanation.surface: A persecutor's reputation might be turned on its head if he were a Christian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversal of' turns the emperor round before he goes into the reputation. A Christian name is a first name, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A first name is traditionally called a Christian name, so a given name may be described that way.

clue.text: With acid about, distance the Guardian from country and western

indicators.note: about means the vitamin word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: folic is the word that goes with acid, as in folic acid
km, kilometres, measures distance
the newspaper speaking of itself says us

explanation.surface: Advice to keep the Guardian and acid away from country music.
explanation.walkthrough: FOLIC goes about KM and US. 'from' is a link. Country and western is a kind of folk music, given loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Country and western grew from the traditional rural music of the American South, a popular strand of traditional song.

clue.text: Check drops for the ear

indicators.note: for the ear means we go by how a word is pronounced

parts.note: rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: Check whether the eardrops are working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' wants to be eardrops; it is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, as a rider does a horse.

clue.text: The top line is a list of people getting some money back

indicators.note: back means the combined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a rota is a list of people taking turns

indicators.note: some means only the first part of the word for money is used

parts.note: remuneration is money paid for work

explanation.surface: A headline about a list of people receiving refunds.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTA then REMUN (part of REMUNERATION), with 'back' reversing the lot: NUMER-ATOR. 'a' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction, the number written above the bar is the top line, with the denominator below.

clue.text: The way people talk of miracle food

indicators.note: people talk of tells us to listen to how the words are spoken

parts.note: a manner is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: People gossip about how a miracle diet works.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'manner' and the food sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus, God sent food from heaven to feed the Israelites in the desert, a miraculous provision.

clue.text: Kind of thinking lacking a thread for dreams coming true

parts.note: wishful thinking is believing what you would like to be true

indicators.note: lacking means the letter given by 'a' is dropped from the thread

parts.note: a filament is a fine thread

explanation.surface: Daydreaming without any connecting thread, yet the dreams come true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' leaves FILMENT; 'Kind of thinking' points at the familiar phrase wishful thinking rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists use the phrase for the imaginary satisfaction of desires, such as dreams in which hopes are realised.

clue.text: Hour passed when people talk

definitions.meaning: a request for the hour is asking what time it is
to pass this with someone means to exchange a few pleasantries

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the current hour, and passing it with someone means a brief friendly chat.

clue.text: Non-U carriage — the right setter's — for agricultural workers

indicators.note: Non-U, the old upper-class label, here literally means the carriage loses its letter U

parts.note: a landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood
R is the usual abbreviation for right
the setter speaking of himself says my

explanation.surface: An unrefined carriage belonging to the setter carries farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' was mid-century slang for not upper-class; here it strips U from LANDAU to leave LANDA. The Land Army sent women to work on British farms in the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Land Army was a wartime body of women drafted to farm labour, hence farm workers.

clue.text: What about … about … about some flowers?

indicators.note: the third about places the short word for concerning inside the rearranged letters
about here means the word What is turned around into a new order

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about flowers, stammering over the same word three times.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' rearranges the word What into WATH, and the third 'about' wraps that round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a ring of flowers and foliage, as laid at a funeral or hung on a door.

clue.text: Wrong end is blue and turned to spray

indicators.note: Wrong suggests these letters are in an incorrect order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Something mistakenly ending up blue has been turned into a fine mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges the nine letters of END IS BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a liquid medicine into a fine mist for inhaling is exactly what an inhaler device does to it.

clue.text: Last year's leaders pledged John Humphrey

indicators.note: leaders tells us to take the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: one who has taken the pledge to give up drink is TT, teetotal
Elton John is the singer

explanation.surface: Last year's leading figures made a promise to a man named John Humphrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'the pledge' meant swearing off alcohol, making one TT. Humphrey Lyttelton was a British jazz trumpeter and radio host.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Lyttelton was the jazz trumpeter and chairman of the BBC radio panel game I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue.

clue.text: Horse of a certain colour died first in its fair town

indicators.note: in places the letter for first inside the fair town

parts.note: Appleby in Cumbria holds a famous annual horse fair
A means first-class, the top grade

explanation.surface: A horse of a particular colour died first at the fair in its home town.
explanation.walkthrough: Appleby Horse Fair in Cumbria is a big gathering of travellers trading horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dapple-bay is a reddish-brown horse marked with darker or lighter spots.

clue.text: It's understood if pet's returned first

indicators.note: first says the turned-round pet comes before the other word
returned means the pet's name is written back to front

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
It is taken as written, the apostrophe-s giving no letters

explanation.surface: It is accepted without saying, provided a pet comes home first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns CAT into TAC, and 'first' puts it ahead of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood or implied without being stated.

clue.text: Letters intended for reproduction as old fashioned protection

definitions.meaning: letters each recipient is asked to copy and send on, as in a chain letter
armour of interlinked metal rings worn in the Middle Ages

explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both chain letters passed on by copying and medieval armour made of linked rings.

clue.text: Twist away with others

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Wriggling free from a group of other people.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench something from someone is to pull or twist it away by force.

clue.text: Restrict amount of sodium amid uncertainties in Biblical town

parts.note: to cap is to put an upper limit on an amount

indicators.note: amid places the chemical symbol in the middle of the hesitation sounds

parts.note: er and um are the noises of a hesitant speaker
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: A health warning about limiting salt in the diet, oddly linked to the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrict amount' reads as part of a salt warning but is a separate piece. Capernaum is a town by the Sea of Galilee in the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Capernaum, on the Sea of Galilee, is where the Gospels place much of Jesus's ministry.

clue.text: Attend to small boy, first to go in

indicators.note: to go in tells us the ordinal is placed inside the boy's name

parts.note: Len is a shortened form of Leonard, a little name for a boy
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Taking care of a little boy who is first to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1' of 1ST is read as the letter I, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed or give attention to someone is to hear them out, the same as attending to them.

clue.text: Scots girl from Zimbabwe

definitions.meaning: a girl's name popular in Scotland
belonging to the main Bantu people and language of Zimbabwe

explanation.definitionFit: The name is a Scottish girl's name and also that of Zimbabwe's largest ethnic group and language.

clue.text: Dance gives priest company

parts.note: a flamen was a priest in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A dance invites the priest to join the party.
explanation.walkthrough: A flamen was a priest of a particular god in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian dance and music style.

clue.text: Time to go?

definitions.meaning: a month of the year is a period of time
to walk in step, like soldiers, is to proceed or go

explanation.definitionFit: It names the third month of the year and the verb for walking with a steady military stride.

clue.text: Bit of a beast, bit of a beast

definitions.meaning: a bit with a chain under the horse's jaw, used to restrain it
a hard swelling on the back of a horse's hock, a part of the animal

explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads it as a mongrel dog plus B; the double reading uses every word, both senses being horse terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a kind of bit for a horse and also a swelling on a horse's leg.

clue.text: Name Shakespeare hero's lost love capturing Tom and queen in place of Hotspur

indicators.note: capturing means the trimmed hero's name holds the next pieces inside it
lost means the hero's name loses the letter standing for love

parts.note: Orlando is the hero of As You Like It
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Naming a Shakespearean hero who lost his love and caught a man and a queen where Hotspur lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost love' leaves ORLAND. Hotspur, Henry Percy in Henry IV Part 1, was heir to the Earl of Northumberland, a county in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Hotspur was son of the Earl of Northumberland, the north-eastern English county ruled by the Percys.

clue.text: Nice day, wrote Scottish Spooner, for song

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the sounds of words, here using the Scots word for nice

parts.note: bonny is the Scots word for pretty or nice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer named Spooner remarks on a fine day in a song lyric.
explanation.walkthrough: BONNY DAY with the opening syllables swapped, BO and DA, gives DANNY BOY: a near-Spoonerism, as the blog says.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny Boy is the famous ballad sung to the Londonderry Air.

clue.text: Girl with tree that may be hocked

definitions.meaning: add hock to this evergreen and you get the tall garden flower hollyhock

explanation.definitionFit: Holly is both a girl's name and the prickly evergreen tree that, with hock added, makes a garden flower.
